---
title: "Installation"
---

## Prerequisites

Always required:

- **Python 3.12+**
- **[uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)** — the package and tool manager
- **git** — the commit/revert flow depends on the target being a git repo

Plus **one or both** AI backends, depending on which team you run:

- **Claude** — the Claude Agent SDK with a working `claude` CLI login
- **GitHub Copilot** — the Copilot SDK with a working `copilot` CLI login

## Install autosprint

Clone the repo and install it as an editable tool so the `autosprint` command
is on your PATH from any directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/haakonbull/autosprint.git
cd autosprint
uv tool install --editable .
```

The install is editable, so pulling a newer autosprint takes effect
immediately. If `pyproject.toml` dependencies changed, reinstall, then refresh
the bundled skills in any target repo you have already initialised:

```bash
uv tool install --editable . --reinstall
autosprint init --update-skills    # run inside the target repo
```

## Verify the setup

From inside a target repository, run the doctor — it checks the target repo,
`destination.md`, the required CLIs, and performs an agent round-trip:

```bash
autosprint doctor
```

## Developing autosprint itself

The development toolchain is driven by `uv` and enforced by
[prek](https://github.com/j178/prek) (a drop-in pre-commit runner):

```bash
uv sync                 # install deps incl. the dev group
prek install            # wire up the git hooks
prek install -t commit-msg
uv run pytest           # run the test suite
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ty check src     # type check
uv run lint-imports     # enforce the layered architecture
```

::: {.callout-note}
Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/);
the `commitlint` hook enforces this on the commit message.
:::
